notes.title: 🔶 Scope 3 Update 1.0.5 – PTT Key Switching and More PTT Keys 🔶
notes.notes:
[p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/e009f3c5700701275819e2c8fef63dae1cd0d2ef.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]🔶 This is Mrsmithentop with Scope 3 Update 1.0.5, and this one delivers [b]PTT key switching[/b] and [b]more PTT keys[/b].[/h1][h1][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/1d29eb88acfa3f1e4caf63d1ffd823f24f1cc13b.png"][/img][/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/47787ad8ea18798b71924bd99b325620775faaef.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]🔶 [b]Choose 1, 2, or 3 push-to-talk keys.[/b]
🔶 [b]Assign a Switch Key[/b] to toggle between them, press it, and Scope 3 cycles.
🔶 [b]Or assign a single PTT key[/b] with no switch[/p][p][/p][h1][b]🔶 What’s New in v1.0.5[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]🔶 [b]Key Switch System (Multi-PTT Cycling)[/b]
You can now assign three separate PTT keys. Tap your Switch Key to cycle between them instantly.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/cb11cc9e440617c8630a2b5caa809bd3a3183c60.png"][/img][/p][p]🔶 Need a different PTT key for multiple games?
🔶 Need to rotate between in-game and Discord keys?
🔶 Need to switch between Squad Chat, Command Chat, and Proxy Chat?[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h1]🔶 [b]How to Use PTT Key Switching (Easy Steps)[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]🔶 [b]1. Open the PTT Panel[/b]
Click the [b]Auto Push-to-Talk[/b] label in Scope 3.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/3afc6b39f93e7e09b542e3db04445083f7e45f79.png"][/img][/p][p]🔶 [b]2. Pick Your Keys[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]One key only?[/b] Set [b]PTT Key 1[/b] and leave Keys 2 & 3 on “N/A.”[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/9cf8029f202ecd9e09e878d915cb1178d50420c4.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]Two keys?[/b] Set [b]PTT Key 1[/b] and [b]PTT Key 2[/b], leave Key 3 on “N/A.”[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/2dcd86d992e640d21c0954538f584198d65f2bb1.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]Three keys?[/b] Set [b]PTT Key 1[/b], [b]PTT Key 2[/b], and [b]PTT Key 3[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/20282c3fbd9521fc23d28b81a40e4580672e575b.png"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p]🔶 [b]3. Assign Your Switch Key (if using >1 key)[/b][/p][list][*][p]If you chose [b]more than one PTT key[/b], pick an unused key from the [b]Switch Key[/b] dropdown. Press it to cycle through your keys.[/p][/*][*][p]If you assigned [b]ONLY ONE[/b] PTT key, leave [b]Switch Key[/b] set to “N/A.”[/p][/*][/list][p]🔶 [b]4. Adjust Mic Sensitivity[/b]
Drag the slider’s triangle to just below where you begin speaking—the [b]meter bar[/b] will guide you. Once it’s locked in, leave it there. It’ll remember its position after closing.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/59c0ee0e351800bcad06cca17eda828b29d21606.png"][/img][/p][p]🔶 [b]5. Switch & Talk[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]One key:[/b] Just speak—you’re live.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Multiple keys:[/b] Press your Switch Key to switch between your keys, then speak.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/bf143b5bcc882010df9478b1471e4f1bca8c43ec.png"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p]🔶 [b]6. Stay Locked In[/b]
Settings save automatically—dominate with hands-free comms.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]🔶 Got feedback? Drop it.
🔶 Found a bug? We want it.
🔶 Got questions? Ask away.
🔶 Got vision? Bring it.[/p][p]This isn’t just an app.
It’s a [b]movement[/b].
And if you’re reading this — you’re already part of it.[/p][p]Join the [url="https://discord.gg/USCcpHmVfP"]Scope 3 Discord[/url][/p][p]Build with us. Shape what’s next. [b]Be louder than silence[/b][/p][p][/p][p]🔶 And that’s our arsenal for today. Scope 3 1.0.5 is locked, loaded, and ready for action. Gear up, take point, and own every comm. Over and out.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/1f3071d9f8ca3646d920f026e8ba4e349979ad9f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: 🔶MRSMITHENTOP'S LETTER🔶
notes.notes:
[h1]🔶🔶🔶MRSMITHENTOP'S LETTER🔶🔶🔶[/h1][p][/p][previewyoutube="GNBtMY410L0;full"][/previewyoutube][h3]🔶🔶🔶 TEXT VERSION🔶🔶🔶[/h3][p][/p][p][b]🔶 Page One – A Message from Mr smithentop[/b][/p][p]Hey everyone,[/p][p]I want to take a moment and speak directly to all of you — the Scope 3 community, the testers, the early adopters, the curious, the committed. This isn’t just another product update. This is something bigger.[/p][p]You’ve seen Scope 3 grow from a focused tool to a serious piece of software. You’ve seen how every update comes from user needs — not hype, not marketing fluff, but precision. I’ve built Scope 3 to solve real problems for real players. It's clean, respectful of game integrity, and it always stays in its lane.[/p][p]But lately, there's been confusion. Another product has appeared on the scene, one that looks and sounds remarkably similar. Their branding, their name, their namespace — all echo mine. The difference? They came after.[/p][p]Let me make this perfectly clear:[/p][p]🔶 [b]Scope 3 is the original.[/b]
🔶 [b]Scope 3 is legally protected.[/b]
🔶 [b]Scope 3 is mine — and always will be.[/b][/p][p]Some of you noticed. Some of you even reached out confused, thinking their work was mine. It wasn’t. What you’re seeing is [b]brand dilution[/b] — and behind the scenes, I’ve had to take action to protect this thing we’ve built together.[/p][p]I’ve filed DMCA takedowns. I’ve responded to impersonation attempts. I’ve documented the use of my marketing language, even my versioning style. I’ve watched developers from the other camp show up in my Discord pretending to be customers, demanding I market more — not to help me, but to lift [b]their[/b] app by confusing the space.[/p][p]But I’m not here to rant. I’m here to clarify.[/p][p]Scope 3 is built with surgical intent. I’m in direct contact with game developers to ensure it remains in fair standing. No one gets banned for using Scope 3. We don’t inject. We don’t modify. We don’t cheat.[/p][p]And now we’re adding [b]Auto Push-To-Talk[/b], an extension I designed myself — not suggested by the community, but created to serve it. It gives streamers, competitive players, and focused communicators a way to keep their mic responsive without holding down a key, while still respecting game audio rules.[/p][p]What we’re building here is about [b]trust, clarity, and function[/b]. Not shortcuts. Not hype. Not deception.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]🔶 Page Two – Scope 3 vs Brand Cloning: Facts You Need to Know[/b][/p][p]This page isn’t about drama — it’s about clarity and protection of our identity.[/p][p]When I launched Scope 3, I didn’t just build an app. I built a namespace, a signature posture, and a community-centered design philosophy. Everything — from the name to the UI, from the release strategy to the user support — was developed in-house and in full alignment with fair use, platform compliance, and original identity.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 I Engineered Scope 3 from Scratch[/b][/p][p]Scope 3 was [b]not cloned[/b], copied, or borrowed.
I built it — [b]personally[/b].[/p][p]Every line of logic, every UI decision, every tool integration came from my own research, testing, and intent. I engineered Scope 3 to solve a very real problem: gamers leaning into their screens, squinting for clarity, breaking posture just to stay competitive. This wasn’t some spin-off of another product. This was — and is — [b]a unique solution[/b] I designed for [b]real users[/b] with [b]real needs[/b].[/p][p]From idea to prototype to release, Scope 3 is [b]100% authored by me[/b] — [b]Mrsmithentop[/b] — without the help or influence of any outside product or company. That’s what makes these clone attempts so offensive. They didn’t just borrow an idea — they tried to [b]confuse users into believing it came from the same place[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 What Happened?[/b][/p][p]A separate product — [b]Scope X[/b] — appeared after Scope 3’s release, replicating several of our core presentation elements:[/p][list][*][p]The [b]“Scope”[/b] naming structure, directly overlapping our namespace.[/p][/*][*][p]UI and UX designs eerily similar to Scope 3's modular layout.[/p][/*][*][p]Marketing headlines and update formats mimicking our tone and structure.[/p][/*][*][p]Discord behavior from related parties mimicking our phrasing and support posture.[/p][/*][/list][p]To the untrained eye, this may have looked like coincidence. But when stacked together, the overlaps created a market identity conflict — legally known as [b]brand dilution[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 Why Brand Dilution Is Serious[/b][/p][p]In trademark and copyright law, [b]“first use in commerce”[/b] carries weight. The party who launches first and uses a namespace publicly in commercial context holds rights over that space, especially if confusion or damage results from imitation.[/p][p]Scope 3 was first.
Scope 3 was public.
Scope 3 was documented.
Scope 3 was established before Scope X existed.[/p][p]Brand dilution is when a competing product tries to adopt similar branding in order to siphon trust, attention, or user association from an existing brand. It confuses customers. It undermines clarity. And it causes reputational harm.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 What We've Seen[/b][/p][p]Some users who tried Scope X reached out to me, directly asking:[/p][p]"Will I get banned for using Scope 3 too?"
"Is Scope 3 a rebrand of Scope X or are you the same developer?"[/p][p]These are not isolated cases. [b]Multiple users[/b] expressed worry after [b]Scope X was warned in certain game communities[/b] for being unauthorized or improperly interacting with games. This confusion affects our credibility — and that’s not acceptable.[/p][p]Scope 3 has [b]never[/b] caused a ban.
Scope 3 has [b]never[/b] been flagged as unsafe.
Scope 3 is [b]built with cooperation[/b] in mind, not exploitation.[/p][p]I personally speak with game developers to ensure we remain on safe, collaborative ground — never stepping on terms of service or fair play boundaries.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 My Legal Response[/b][/p][p]This isn’t something I take lightly.[/p][p]✔️ I’ve issued [b]formal DMCA takedowns[/b] against cloned assets and branding violations.
✔️ I’m maintaining full documentation of visual and structural similarities.
✔️ I have legal conversations ongoing, but I’ll let the results speak when the time is right.
✔️ I’ve archived impersonation efforts — including members associated with Scope X entering our Discord, [b]pretending to be customers[/b], and trying to [b]pressure me into marketing more[/b]… not for our growth, but to cover up their shortfalls.[/p][p]These aren’t conspiracy theories. These are timestamped, archived facts.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 Where We Draw the Line[/b][/p][p]Scope 3 is about [b]innovation[/b], not imitation.[/p][p]We build [b]clean[/b], [b]ethical[/b], [b]high-performance[/b] tools that respect the games you love and the platforms we release on. We [b]don’t get users banned[/b], we don’t step outside legal boundaries, and we don’t impersonate.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔸 I’m Not Just Defending Scope 3 — I’m Defending You[/b][/p][p]This project is about giving you tools that feel like an extension of your own gameplay style. Tools that make sense. That respect your setups. That never put your accounts or games at risk.[/p][p]That’s why we draw the line so clearly — and stand by it.[/p][p] [/p][p] [/p][p][b]🔶 Page Three – From the Trenches of Esports: Why Scope 3 Had to Exist[/b][/p][p]Let me take you back. Before Scope 3. Before the noise, the copycats, the community, and even the tool itself—there was just me.[/p][p]A competitive player, climbing the ranks the hard way.[/p][p]I wasn’t a prodigy. I didn’t have flashy sponsors or viral clips. What I had was discipline. Grind. And pain.[/p][p]Lots of it.[/p][p]I entered esports with fire, but I didn’t make it through on passion alone. I had coaches—real ones—who broke me down to milliseconds and micro-movements. It wasn’t just about playing the game. It was about playing it in a [b]hyper-optimized, inhumanly efficient way[/b], until that method of play [i]became me[/i].[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 The Pressure You Never See on Stream[/b][/p][p]Imagine having your coach freeze footage to correct your [b]eyeball drift[/b].
Or being told that a [b]half-inch head tilt[/b] was the reason you lost a clutch.
That your [b]reaction time dropped by 6ms[/b] because your neck wasn’t at the right tension angle.[/p][p]That was my world.[/p][p]This wasn’t just keyboard and mouse. This was a machine — and I was one of the parts. I was taught [b]eye tracking drills[/b], [b]reaction pattern loops[/b], [b]eyestreaming discipline[/b], and [b]postural lock-ins[/b] that had to hold through six-hour scrims.[/p][p]Eyestreaming — the heart of what makes Scope 3 possible — was an [b]unspoken secret[/b] in those rooms.[/p][p]We trained our eyes to [b]scan the screen[/b] edge-to-edge without moving the mouse.
We ran drills that mimicked eye saccades—those micro-jerks your eyes make—to [b]increase cognitive processing[/b] across multiple HUD elements.
We were tested on how long we could scan five information zones while holding [b]muscular tension in the jaw and neck[/b] to prevent posture loss.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 And Then the Pain Came[/b][/p][p]At first, I ignored it. Everyone did.
Neck stiffness? “Stretch more.”
Eye blur? “Blink less.”
Tension headaches? “Sleep better.”[/p][p]But the truth is, [b]we were injuring ourselves for the sake of awareness[/b].[/p][p]It caught up to me hard:[/p][list][*][p]🔶 My neck started locking during games.[/p][/*][*][p]🔶 My left shoulder became numb after sessions.[/p][/*][*][p]🔶 I got dizzy after long sessions due to oculomotor fatigue.[/p][/*][*][p]🔶 My back curved from [b]years of leaning into the screen[/b] unconsciously.[/p][/*][*][p]🔶 My emotional regulation dipped from chronic [b]sympathetic overload[/b] (fight or flight).[/p][/*][/list][p]At tournaments, I’d go from stage lights and adrenaline straight into near blackout migraines.
I was fighting for milliseconds — and it was taking [b]years off my physical wellness[/b].[/p][p]And no one knew.
No one saw.
Because these aren’t the battle scars people talk about.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 Why Scope 3 Was Born[/b][/p][p]Scope 3 was never some experiment in power. It was born from that [b]quiet suffering[/b] — the kind only [b]serious players[/b] understand.[/p][p]I wanted a tool that [b]gave me back what I lost[/b].[/p][p]I engineered Scope 3 not to boost performance, but to [b]stop the decay[/b].[/p][list][*][p]So others didn’t have to bend forward to feel “locked in”[/p][/*][*][p]So players didn’t have to destroy their necks to keep control[/p][/*][*][p]So competitive clarity could be brought to the [b]average player[/b], without physical cost[/p][/*][*][p]So that [b]eyestreaming precision[/b] could be simulated without years of neural programming[/p][/*][/list][p]And it works.[/p][p]But I get it — to someone who hasn’t trained this way, Scope 3 can seem alien.
Even… suspicious.
Like, “Why does it look like this? Why does it feel different?”[/p][p]Because it’s replicating a [b]style of gameplay[/b] that used to live only in the [b]bodies of the broken[/b].[/p][p]Scope 3 simulates [b]what pro players put their bodies through[/b], minus the harm.
That’s why it’s unfamiliar. That’s why it’s powerful.
That’s why it’s necessary.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 Balance, Not Advantage[/b][/p][p]Let me be absolutely clear:[/p][p]Scope 3 is balanced. Period.[/p][p]Each zoom level is [b]engineered[/b] to provide clarity — not dominance. The system avoids competitive gaps by:[/p][list][*][p]Capping max zoom intelligently[/p][/*][*][p]Keeping overlays minimal[/p][/*][*][p]Offering equal visibility profiles across every option[/p][/*][*][p]And enforcing stability between mouse vs. keyboard control preferences[/p][/*][/list][p]Nobody using Scope 3 gets an edge over someone else — but they [b]do get relief[/b].[/p][p]That’s the goal.[/p][p]Not to take from others — but to give back what competition takes from us:
[b]Our health. Our posture. Our peace.[/b][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 From My Body, To Yours[/b][/p][p]I built this because [b]I had to[/b].
Because I couldn’t do it anymore.
Because I knew I wasn’t the only one breaking their body to stay in the game.[/p][p]I’m not just a developer.
I’m one of you.
I played until it broke me — then I built a tool that would [b]stop others from breaking too[/b].[/p][p]Scope 3 is the tool I wish I had when I needed it most.[/p][p]And now, it’s yours.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]🔶 Page Four – Respect, Not Rebellion: The Developer’s Line I Refuse to Cross[/b][/p][p]Let me shift focus — from esports, to engineering.[/p][p]From the moment Scope 3 went from personal necessity to public release, I knew what kind of developer I wanted to be.[/p][p]Not someone trying to fly under the radar.
Not someone bypassing detection systems.
And never — never — someone who risks a player's account or reputation just to push out a feature faster.[/p][p]This is where Scope 3 draws a hard line:
[b]I work with the spirit of the games — not against them.[/b][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 I Talk to Developers — A Lot[/b][/p][p]Every feature I add is weighed with care, because Scope 3 isn’t just software — it’s a promise to do things the right way.[/p][p]That means:[/p][list][*][p]🔸 I have open conversations with game developers[/p][/*][*][p]🔸 I listen carefully to their concerns around competitive integrity[/p][/*][*][p]🔸 I avoid any feature that introduces exploitable behavior[/p][/*][*][p]🔸 Scope 3 never injects into games, hooks game processes, or impersonates system inputs[/p][/*][*][p]🔸 Everything it does runs [b]externally, transparently[/b], and [b]ethically[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]That's why no Scope 3 user has been banned.
And that's by [b]design[/b] — not luck.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 Where Scope X Crossed the Line — And Why It Matters[/b][/p][p]This isn’t a rivalry.
This isn’t competition.
[b]This is about integrity.[/b][/p][p]Scope X released a set of features that [b]go beyond ergonomic assistance and into unfair mechanical advantage[/b] — things I explicitly chose [b]not[/b] to implement, because I’ve spoken directly with developers and understand the risks.[/p][p]Their version introduces:[/p][list][*][p]Unauthorized visual augmentations[/p][/*][*][p]Game-facing manipulation layers[/p][/*][*][p]Input behavior that mimics assisted targeting[/p][/*][/list][p]These things [b]do not align with esports ethics[/b] or developer guidelines.
They create an imbalance — and [b]developers notice[/b].[/p][p]The result?[/p][list][*][p]Players using Scope X have been banned in certain games[/p][/*][*][p]Developers are forced to grow suspicious of any tool that bears the name "Scope"[/p][/*][*][p]And [b]my ability to build relationships and partnerships is damaged[/b] — despite having done nothing wrong[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 Scope 3 Is Not an Overlay, Cheat, or Exploit[/b][/p][p]Scope 3 doesn’t patch drivers.
It doesn’t alter memory.
It doesn’t hide behind DLL tricks or overlays.[/p][p]It is a [b]purely external tool[/b] — just like Discord or OBS — that exists beside your game, not inside it.
Its focus is [b]posture, clarity, and physical well-being[/b], not advantage.[/p][p]Because I understand how small edge cases can ripple into ban systems,
and I [b]refuse to play that game[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 Brand Contamination Hurts Real Work[/b][/p][p]When Scope X mimics Scope 3’s name, layout, and posture — then adds [b]unauthorized, risky features[/b] — it doesn’t just confuse players.[/p][p]It [b]damages everything I’ve built[/b].[/p][list][*][p]Developers now question the word "Scope"[/p][/*][*][p]My product gets lumped into risk lists by association[/p][/*][*][p]Players are afraid to use Scope 3 because of bans caused by another team’s reckless design[/p][/*][/list][p]I built Scope 3 with discipline.
I left power on the table — [b]on purpose[/b] — to protect you.[/p][p]Scope X didn’t. And now [b]you see the difference[/b][/p][p] [/p][p][b]🔶 Page Five – The Unbreakable Origin[/b][/p][p]This is not a confession.
This is a [b]declaration[/b].[/p][p]Scope 3 wasn’t born from shortcuts.
It was built from [b]discipline[/b], [b]vision[/b], and [b]resolve[/b].
No templates. No cloning. No borrowed blueprints.[/p][p]And now that it’s here —
[b]It will not be moved.[/b][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 My Work Stands Alone[/b][/p][p]Scope 3 is engineered.
I designed every mechanism. Every customization. Every layer of fairness baked into it was [b]intentional[/b].[/p][p]I didn’t follow trends. I didn’t rush to market.
I built something that would last — something that [b]couldn’t be mistaken[/b] if you’ve ever actually used it.[/p][p]Others didn’t build. They followed.
They copied names, copied aesthetics, and [b]positioned themselves inside my namespace[/b].[/p][p]This isn’t a rivalry. This is someone [b]squatting on identity[/b] —
Trying to occupy the same air, without breathing the same fire.[/p][p]Let them.
Because [b]nothing about Scope 3 is replicable.[/b][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 I’ve Seen Their Play — and I Wrote the Counter[/b][/p][p]They came under disguise.
Infiltrated my community.
Demanded I “market more” so [b]their clone could grow behind my momentum[/b].[/p][p]That’s not business.
That’s not competition.
That’s a parasite trying to feed on origin.[/p][p]But here's the problem with shadowing giants:
[b]You never grow your own stride.[/b][/p][p]Scope 3 is recognized because it doesn't take shortcuts — and neither do I.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 The Standard You Can’t Touch[/b][/p][p]I didn’t build Scope 3 to cheat systems.
I built it to [b]respect them[/b] —
While fixing what most people didn’t even realize was broken.[/p][p]Neck fatigue.
Eye exhaustion.
The micro-movements that wear you down after 1,000 hours of pushing your limits.[/p][p]That’s what Scope 3 is for:
[b]Real correction. Real relief. Real playability.[/b][/p][p]It doesn’t break games — it restores gamers.
It doesn’t trigger bans — it earns trust.
It’s not flagged — it’s [b]welcomed[/b].[/p][p]Because I took the time to make sure it fits into the ecosystem without bending the rules.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 This Is Not a Defense. This Is a Warning.[/b][/p][p]To my users:
You are protected. You are seen. You are using the tool [b]everyone else is trying to catch up to.[/b][/p][p]To the copycats:
You're not standing beside me.
You're standing [b]in my trail.[/b][/p][p]And to the industry:
Understand the difference between a [b]tool of alleviation[/b] and a [b]tool of advantage[/b].
I’ve had those conversations. I’ll continue to have them.
And Scope 3 will continue to stand on solid ground.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]🔶 I’m Not Just the Creator — I’m the Guardian[/b][/p][p]This is more than product protection.
It’s about [b]preserving standards[/b].[/p][p]I’ve already begun legal operations behind the scenes — and I’ll escalate where necessary.
I don’t need to shout. I need to finish the work.
And I will.[/p][p]This is about legacy.
It’s about showing that [b]when you stand for something, it holds.[/b][/p][p]Scope 3 is not a reaction.
It’s the [b]benchmark[/b].
It’s the [b]original[/b].
It’s the [b]real one[/b].[/p][p]And it does not yield.[/p][p]– [b]Mr smithentop[/b][/p][p] [/p][h1] 🔶🔶🔶 LEADING UP TO THIS 🔶🔶🔶[/h1][p][/p][h3]🔶FAZE 1🔶⤵️[/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="1U4brFW1Luc;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h3]🔶FAZE 2🔶⤵️[/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="pq3tv_G4QyI;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h3]🔶FAZE 3🔶⤵️[/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="ULhw_IG5FMM;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h3]🔶FAZE 4🔶⤵️[/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="emiAk8RSRbo;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/1f3071d9f8ca3646d920f026e8ba4e349979ad9f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: 🔶 Scope 3 Update 1.0.4 – Introducing Auto Push-to-Talk 🔶
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/058b2ed998f182fb25b10450cdf9a561a39a1404.png"][/img][/p][p]This is Mrsmithentop, bringing you Scope 3 Update 1.0.4.
With this version, I’m releasing something I've been personally working on—an official addon to Scope 3: [b]Auto Push-to-Talk[/b].[/p][p]This isn't based on community suggestion—this one comes straight from me.
It's designed for games that [i]require[/i] Push-to-Talk, and it’s perfect for streamers and players who want to stay locked in.
Now, you can speak freely and let Scope 3 handle the keypress.[/p][p]🔶 What's New[/p][p]🔶 Auto Push-to-Talk (v1.0.1)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/e3b96d134654641ef1f33edae622ca3d6a73b749.png"][/img]Auto PTT is now bundled as an optional addon in Scope 3.
It monitors your mic level in real time, and when it hears your voice, it presses your chosen key for you—automatically.[/p][p]🔶 Precision Slider for Sensitivity
Set it and forget it. Move the slider to your preferred mic threshold.
It’ll activate [i]only[/i] when you speak at or above your chosen level.[/p][p]🔶 Full Key Support
Use any key on your keyboard as your push-to-talk trigger.
Scope 3 will press and release it automatically based on your voice input.[/p][p]🔶 Built for Voice-Centric Games
This feature is specifically made for games where push-to-talk is the only option.
It’s hands-free, seamless, and made to feel native.
Whether you’re streaming or squad-leading, your hands stay focused while Scope 3 does the talking.[/p][p]🔶 How to Use Auto Push-to-Talk[/p][p]Click the [b]Auto Push-to-Talk[/b] label to launch the addon.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/3afc6b39f93e7e09b542e3db04445083f7e45f79.png"][/img]From there:[/p][p]🔶 Select your [b]microphone[/b] from the dropdown[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/5f433443fa583951a27311407bffdfe5d116a98a.png"][/img][/p][p]🔶 Choose the [b]key[/b] you want it to trigger[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/4010439938f31a1eeb296d222c10074c9852c3cb.png"][/img][/p][p]🔶 [b]Speak[/b] your voice will activate the key[/p][p]🔶 Adjust the [b]sensitivity slider[/b] to where it feels right for you[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/59c0ee0e351800bcad06cca17eda828b29d21606.png"][/img][/p][p]No save button needed. It remembers your settings.[/p][p]🔶 This One's Personal
This is a feature I designed because it was missing in every tool I tested.
Scope 3 now has it, and it’s better, faster, and tailored for real-time game response.[/p][p]🔶 Community & Reporting[/p][p]This is Auto PTT version 1.0.1, part of Scope 3 version 1.0.4.
If you run into any issues, I need you to report it on Discord.
We're shaping this tool together. You lay the landscape—I’ll build on it.[/p][p]🔗 [url="https://discord.gg/USCcpHmVfP"]Join the Scope 3 Discord[/url][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/f3096fa7b1567f326dc86889e7e0172361f45d35.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/c0cf71eef37a5169c07094aba51d1fd8d4b0d1a3.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/1f3071d9f8ca3646d920f026e8ba4e349979ad9f.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: 🔶Scope 3 Update 1.0.3 – Back & Forward Buttons Now Work🔶
notes.notes:
🔶 Scope 3 Update 1.0.3 – Expanded Mouse Support + Keybind Stability

Version 1.0.3 delivers a precision-focused upgrade built entirely around user requests. For those who prefer using their mouse’s Back or Forward buttons to zoom, this update is for you.

🔶 What’s New

🔶 Back & Forward Button Support
You can now assign your mouse’s Back and Forward buttons to control zoom.
No workarounds. No remapping. Just clean support for users who rely on those side buttons for comfort and speed.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/29448fb1eba8b41b4eb7f6eceab2ce89f3d39ce9.png[/img]

🔶 Automatic Settings Saving
Scope 3 now remembers your exact setup — mouse, keyboard, and zoom mode preferences — the moment you close the app.
Everything stays locked in for next time. No need to reset anything.

🔶 Why We Update
We hear you.
Every Scope 3 update is small by design, focused only on meaningful features.

🔶 You Shaped This Update
The addition of Back and Forward button support came directly from user feedback.
Scope 3 evolves based on how real people use it — not assumptions. Keep the ideas coming.

🔶 Join the Scope 3 Discord
Share suggestions, connect with other users, and help shape what’s next.
We’re building Scope 3 with precision — and with you.

🔗 https://discord.gg/USCcpHmVfP

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/8596250b6fc4cd5cb75cb37b97abd0479d4013d8.png[/img]

🔶 Scope 3 Update Summary – Keybind Optimizations + More

We’ve rolled out a powerful new update to Scope 3, bringing faster zoom control, automatic saving, and for the first time ever, controller support!

🔶 What's New

🔶 Xbox Controller Support is Here! 🎮
We're proud to announce that Scope 3 now fully supports Xbox controllers.
Take control like never before. Assign your favorite button, zoom instantly, and experience a whole new level of precision and comfort.
Scope 3 is no longer just for keyboard and mouse. Grab your controller and feel the difference.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/edd9532ce5e03622e1f70fcbbb68e0533a23d5a2.png[/img]

🔶 Lightning-Fast Keybind Reaction
We've fine-tuned the P + O and P + L hotkeys to respond faster than ever, delivering smoother transitions between zoom modes when you need it most.

🔶 Automatic Settings Saving
Scope 3 now automatically saves your keyboard, mouse, and controller settings the moment you close the app.
No more setting up every time. Your preferences stay locked in and ready.

🔶 Our Update Philosophy
Every update we release is intentionally small, strategic, and tested with care.
We believe in keeping Scope 3 balanced, fair, and optimized for real-world gameplay, not just in the lab.

🔶 We Want Your Feedback
Scope 3 grows stronger because of you.
Every idea, every suggestion, every piece of feedback helps shape the future of the project. Thank you for being a crucial part of this journey.

🔶 Join Our Discord
Help us build the next chapter of Scope 3. Share your ideas, suggest improvements, and meet others who believe in gaming with precision.

notes.title: SCOPE 3 UPDATE 1.0.1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45277420/6b66aeb97492f82b9c96aa4c76399e194620fbfa.png[/img]

🔶 **Scope 3 Update Summary – Full Keyboard Support + More**

We’ve rolled out a fresh update to Scope 3 with new features designed with precision and community feedback in mind.

🔶 **What's New**

🔶 **Full Keyboard Support**  
You can now use every keyboard key as a valid trigger for zoom actions in Scope 3.

🔶 **Press P + O to enable or disable zoom instantly.**  
🔶 **Press P + L to activate toggle zoom mode.**

🔶 **Our Update Philosophy**  
Every update we release is intentionally small and strategic.  
We do this out of respect for game developers and to ensure Scope 3 remains a tactically balanced tool.  
We carefully test each integration to keep it fair, stable, and community-driven.

🔶 **We Want Your Feedback**  
Join our official Discord and help shape the future of Scope 3:  
https://discord.gg/USCcpHmVfP

Your support, ideas, and suggestions are what make Scope 3 stronger. Thank you for continuing to stand behind us and being part of the journey.

🔶 **Zoom Centering Fix (Common Issue)**  
If you’re experiencing off-center zooming:

🔶 Go to your Windows Display Settings  
🔶 Set Display Scaling to 100%

This ensures proper centering and accuracy when zooming.

notes.notes:
Scope 3 is out be sure to join our Discord: https://discord.gg/tD95m3aG5v To input your suggestions ideas or the development of Scope 3


Scope 3 Summary:

I’ve been passionately working on Scope 3 for the past 8 years, driven by a commitment to creating a tool that enhances the way we interact with games. This has been a labor of love, refined and improved over nearly a decade, and it brings me immense joy to finally share it with you. Scope 3 is an incredible tool tailored to elevate your gaming experience, particularly in flight simulators and first-person shooters.

Whether you're navigating the skies or lining up precision shots, Scope 3 offers unparalleled support to make every detail crystal clear. Designed with comfort and functionality in mind, it helps reduce the need to lean into your screen, allowing for a more natural and enjoyable gaming posture. My goal has always been to provide gamers with tools that make their experience smoother and more immersive, and Scope 3 achieves that with precision and reliability.

Thank you for being a part of this journey. It’s been a pleasure and an honor to create something that serves the gaming community so well.
